Title: No Defender for Cloud security contact configured
Summary: Defender for Cloud plans are enabled and well matched to the deployed services, but no security contact exists, so high-severity alerts on this production workload are raised into the portal and never delivered to a responder.
Recommendation: Configure a Defender for Cloud security contact with a monitored distribution list and an alert severity threshold, then route alerts into the incident process and confirm delivery with a test alert.

Title: Recovery has never been tested and achieved RTO and RPO are unknown
Summary: Zone-redundant HA, 35-day geo-redundant database backups and blob point-in-time restore are all configured, but no dated exercise proves a restore has ever been performed or how long it takes.
Recommendation: Run a full restore drill covering database, media, secrets and configuration; measure and publish the achieved RTO and RPO, and record defects and owners against MAN-02.

Title: Origin bypass and WAF enforcement are configured but never tested
Summary: App Service ingress is restricted to the Front Door service tag plus the Front Door identifier header and the WAF runs in Prevention mode, but no negative test proves a request that skips Front Door is refused or that a blocked request produces an investigable log entry.
Recommendation: Run a direct-origin request against the azurewebsites.net host, a WAF block test and a secret-rotation test; retain the results and the corresponding Front Door WAF log entries against MAN-07.

Title: WordPress administration path has no WAF or network restriction
Summary: The only custom WAF rule rate-limits /wp-login.php and /xmlrpc.php at 20 requests per minute per source address. No rule protects /wp-admin and App Service Authentication is disabled, so the administration surface is defended only by WordPress's own password prompt.
Recommendation: Add a WAF rule restricting /wp-admin/* to approved source addresses or an authenticated path, deliberately exempting the admin-ajax.php routes the theme requires, then re-test administrative access.

Title: WordPress dashboard file editing is not disabled
Summary: The app settings collection succeeded and contains no DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT and no explicit WP_DEBUG value, so theme and plugin file editing from the WordPress dashboard remains available. Any administrator compromise therefore becomes remote code execution. phpMyAdmin is correctly disabled.
Evidence: appservice-samplewpprod-wp-prod-sample001.json → sections.appSettings.data (26 names captured; SETUP_PHPMYADMIN = "false"; no DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT, no WP_DEBUG)
Recommendation: Set DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT, set WP_DEBUG explicitly to false rather than relying on the image default, and block /xmlrpc.php outright unless a client requires it.

Title: Recovery windows are inconsistent across database and media
Summary: The database can be restored to any point within 35 days but media point-in-time restore reaches only 29 days and blob soft delete 30 days, so a restore older than 29 days cannot produce a matching database and media state.
Recommendation: Align blob point-in-time restore and soft-delete retention with the 35-day database window, or reduce the database window to the approved RPO, and document the resulting recovery set as a single unit.

Title: No deployment slot so no tested rollback path
Summary: The slots section collected successfully and returned nothing, so no deployment slot exists despite the PremiumV3 plan including slots at no extra cost. Every release lands directly on the production site with no swap-with-preview, no warm-up stage and no instant rollback.
Recommendation: Create a staging slot with slot-specific settings, enable Application Initialization warm-up, and adopt swap with preview so the previous version remains available for an immediate swap back.

Title: Private Link Scope deployed but public monitoring access still enabled
Summary: An Azure Monitor Private Link Scope, an approved private endpoint and four monitor private DNS zones are deployed, yet both the Log Analytics workspace and Application Insights still accept ingestion and queries from the public internet, so the private path is available but not enforced.
Recommendation: Set publicNetworkAccessForIngestion and publicNetworkAccessForQuery to Disabled on both the workspace and Application Insights after confirming every ingestion and query path resolves through the AMPLS.

Title: No approved SLO RTO or RPO to assess resilience spend against
Summary: Nine of thirteen foundations controls could not be decided from collected evidence. Most consequentially no SLO, RTO or RPO is defined, so zone-redundant HA, three-instance capacity and 35-day geo-redundant backups cannot be validated as sufficient or excessive.
Recommendation: Define and approve SLO, RTO and RPO values with the business owner, then re-assess REL-08 through REL-14 and CST-04 against them.

Title: Autoscale profile not captured so scale behaviour is unproven
Summary: An autoscale setting targets the App Service plan but the collector does not capture its profiles, triggers or cooldowns, and maximumElasticWorkerCount equals current capacity, so scale-out headroom cannot be confirmed.
Recommendation: Export the autoscale profile and confirm the minimum instance count is at least three, the zone-redundancy floor, and that headroom exists above the current capacity.

Title: Key Vault secret expiry and rotation could not be verified
Summary: Secrets are demonstrably stored in Key Vault and referenced from the application, but the keys, secrets and certificates sections were refused because the vault is correctly private, so expiry dates, rotation ownership and expiry alerting are unproven.
Evidence: keyvault-kv-sample-wp-prod-sample001.json → sections.secrets.success = false, error = "ERROR: (Forbidden) Connection is not an approved private link…"
Recommendation: Re-run the collector from inside the virtual network, or export secret expiry and rotation evidence manually and exercise a rotation against MAN-06.

Title: No runbooks evidenced for the documented recovery paths
Summary: Twelve of seventeen operational controls could not be decided. No runbook, incident process, IaC repository or drift report was supplied, even though the resource lock notes explicitly reference a documented recovery runbook.
Evidence: resource-group-inventory.json → sections.locks.data notes reference a recovery runbook that was not supplied
Recommendation: Write and attach the runbook set covering failed deployment, WAF false positive, origin bypass, compromised administrator, database restore, cache loss and secret rotation.

Title: No load or soak test proves behaviour at peak traffic
Summary: The caching, scale-out and SKU choices are sound but no load, stress, soak or cache-invalidation test artefact exists, so the workload's actual ceiling and its behaviour at saturation are unknown.
Recommendation: Run an Azure Load Testing suite against production-like critical flows at expected peak and growth traffic, and record the capacity conclusions against MAN-10.

Title: MySQL grant separation not verified
Summary: Microsoft Entra authentication-only is proven at server level, but MySQL grants are not collected so it cannot be confirmed that the application principal is distinct from the server administrator and holds only the privileges it needs.
Recommendation: Export SHOW GRANTS for the application identity, confirm it is not the server administrator, and separate schema migration from application read and write privileges.

Title: Manual validation register is entirely unevidenced
Summary: All twelve mandatory manual-validation items are Not verified because no dated manual evidence was supplied. This is the single largest contributor to the 48% overall coverage figure.
Recommendation: Schedule the twelve manual validations, assign an owner and target date to each, and attach dated evidence so Section 8 can be scored at the next review.

Title: No alerting on email send volume or failures
Summary: Communication Services traffic metrics are collected but none of the eleven metric alerts targets the resource, so a compromised sending identity, a plugin retry storm or contact-form abuse would generate cost and reputational damage with no detection signal.
Evidence: communication-services-sample-wp-prod-acs-sample001.json → sections.diagnosticSettings.data.metrics.category = "Traffic" with no matching metricalert in resource-group-inventory.json
Recommendation: Add a metric alert on send volume and failed sends routed to the existing sample-wp-prod-alerts action group, and set a spend guardrail for the channel.

Title: No budget forecast or anomaly alert for the workload
Summary: Cost hygiene in the resource configuration is strong, but no budget, forecast threshold or anomaly alert was collected, so spend is reviewed only after invoice close.
Recommendation: Create a resource-group budget with forecast and anomaly alerts routed to the existing sample-wp-prod-alerts action group, with a named accountable recipient.
